subject: Private connectivity & SDK integration — post-demo items and next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood demo — quick recap and next technical steps

Hi Elaine — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can unblock an onramp to a private deployment: 

Key demo highlights
- Verified Lumenix needs: low-latency embeddings + reranker for search, structured-tool-calling for downstream enrichment, and strict egress controls for PII workloads.
- We showed a Dedicated/private deployment running the 7B quantized variant with embeddings and structured output enabled.

Immediate asks from your team
1) Can you confirm whether you prefer a VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) or a vendor-managed peering approach for traffic into Redwood?
2) Do you have CIDR ranges for an IP allowlist or a NSG we should expect?
3) Any requirements for mTLS termination (client certs at the edge) vs. mTLS end-to-end to our runtime?
4) Do we need to support custom DNS/egress proxies for third-party calls (webhooks/tool-calls)?

Proposed next steps
- Ben (cc’d) will follow up with a technical onramp doc and an initial list of IP ranges we’ll need for staging and prod.
- Priyom can run a short design session with your infra/security owners to validate mTLS and token-exchange flows.
- I’ll send a one-page checklist and a network diagram for Lumenix to annotate — attaching now.

Attachments: post-demo-checklist.pdf

If you’re available early next week we can lock a 45-min engineering call to walk the network diagram and auth flows. What times work for your infra team?

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

From: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenix.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, security@lumenix.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — quick recap and next technical steps

Aisha — appreciate the recap and the checklist. A few answers and follow-ups from our infra/security side: 

Answers to your asks
- We strongly prefer an AWS PrivateLink endpoint into our VPC (no public IPs for request egress).
- Primary CIDR blocks: 10.12.0.0/16 (prod), 10.18.0.0/16 (staging). We can provide more granular IPs if you require them for firewall rules.
- mTLS: security wants mutual TLS from our side to Redwood (client certs) with Redwood validating client cert CNs. We also require server cert validation on our end for any callbacks.
- DNS/egress: Third-party tool-calls must route through our egress proxy (outbound via 10.18.5.0/24) and preserve SNI — we will not allow direct outbound to arbitrary public hosts from the Redwood runtime.

Attached: lumenix-network-diagram-v1.pdf and a filled security questionnaire (security-questionnaire-filled.csv).

Can Ben and Priyom propose a minimal allowed set of Redwood egress destinations and certificate thumbprint steps? We’d like to lock these before the design call. Also, can you confirm whether your SDK supports native mTLS (client cert store) or if we should use a sidecar/egress gateway?

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Infra Lead, Lumenix
elaine@lumenix.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenix.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — quick recap and next technical steps

Thanks Elaine — good detail. For internal alignment / quick handoff notes (copying Aisha/Priyom/Soojin):

Short plan (technical lead: Priyom)
- Networking: We will provision an AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint in Lumenix VPC. Required inbound: our PrivateLink ENIs will present from AWS-managed addresses; for firewall-friendly rules we will publish a recommended set of endpoint ENI IP ranges (we can give a small CIDR list for allowlisting).
- IP allowlist: Ask Lumenix whether they want allowlisting at per-endpoint ENI level or at a small set of fixed egress IPs we provide from our NAT/egress pool. We prefer the per-environment NAT IP pool approach so we can preserve autoscaling.
- mTLS: Redwood SDK currently supports TLS with client certs via our SDK-native keystore (we recently shipped a client-cert hook). If Lumenix requires termination at your edge, we can support that with a sidecar pattern. Priyom to confirm exact cert exchange steps.
- Auth: Recommend short-lived token exchange (OIDC client credentials at the edge) + per-request signed metadata for tool-calling. No long-lived API keys for prod.
- Tool-calls / structured output: Since Lumenix has egress proxies, we will route webhook/tool-calls via your proxy CIDR and support SNI/proxy-auth headers (we'll add this to the SDK runtime config).

Initial deliverables we will share by Tue 12/08
- redwood_private_onramp_matrix.xlsx (attachment) — mapping of endpoints, ports, cert steps and expected firewall rules.
- Minimal egress destinations list (FQDNs and IPs) and a recommended CIDR set for allowlisting.
- A short runbook for cert thumbprint verification and rotation cadence.

Can Priyom own the 12/08 deliverables? Also recommend a 60-min design call on Wed 12/09 with Lumenix infra + security to sign off. Elaine — does that work?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_private_onramp_matrix.xlsx

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenix.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 17:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — quick recap and next technical steps

Elaine / team — thanks for the details. I’m happy to own the design deliverables and run the Wed 12/09 call. A few technical notes and requested inputs so we can make the call productive: 

Prep items for Lumenix before 12/09 call
- Confirm preferred allowlist model: per-endpoint ENI IPs OR a fixed NAT egress pool. If NAT pool, please provide the production NAT IPs (or confirm you’ll allow dynamic NAT ranges we provide).
- If you will use client certs: provide the CA issuer details and whether certs will be rotated via your in-house PKI or a managed CA. We need the cert CN format to validate in our runtime.
- Indicate whether webhooks/tool-calls must include a custom header for verification at your proxy. If yes, share header name/value pattern.

Design notes for the call
- We plan to demonstrate a short certificate exchange flow using our SDK client-cert hook and a fallback sidecar flow. I’ll include commands for generating a CSR and validating thumbprints.
- For PrivateLink we will show expected flow diagrams for request ingress, and options to preserve client IPs in logs for audit (we support X-Forwarded-For preservation into the tracing pipeline).
- For embeddings/rerankers: we’ll recommend colocating a smaller dedicated GPU pool in your VPC region for <50ms median embedding latency. We’ll show batch sizing and KV cache settings tuned for search workloads.

Action items (owner / ETA)
- Priyom: deliver full matrix + cert runbook + egress list (ETA 2026-12-08).
- Aisha: schedule Wed 12/09 60-min design call w/ Lumenix infra + security (ETA 2026-12-06).
- Ben: prepare cost/throughput estimate for dedicated pool sizing (ETA 2026-12-07).

Links: design doc template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxy-example-docs (I’ll drop the matrix there). HubSpot record: 6789123

If everyone is aligned I’ll circulate the invite after Aisha confirms a time.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Priyom's quick cert command examples (for reference)
# generate CSR
openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout lumenix-client.key -out lumenix-client.csr -subj "/CN=lumenix-client/O=Lumenix"
# verify thumbprint
openssl x509 -in lumenix-client.crt -noout -fingerprint -sha256
